articles.title: Tough times
articles.excerpt: The Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe fleet continues its progress in robust conditions, still reeling from the capsizing of one of the favorites, Armel Le Cléac’h (Maxi Banque Populaire XI, Ultim). This afternoon he was picked up by a Panamanian tanker. He is in good health. The Bank Populaire team have acknowledged of everyone who contributed to his rescue and to those who have been mobilised to recover the boat. Le Cléac’h has a complicated history with this solo ocean sprint.

articles.title: 📸 Selfies of our sailors
articles.excerpt:
Toutes les classes poursuivent leur route à travers l’Atlantique ! Certains skippers naviguent au large des Açores, d’autres approchent de la pointe de l’Espagne… Tous avancent à leur rythme, mais avec un seul et même objectif : rejoindre la Guadeloupe ! 

Entre deux manœuvres, ils prennent le temps d’immortaliser leur aventure. Découvrez leurs derniers clichés envoyés depuis le bord ! 📸⛵

articles.title: Anthony Marchand forced to end his Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe
articles.excerpt: Hope held until the very end. But despite the team's immediate mobilization and the investigations carried out in Galway on Actual Ultim 4, the conditions are not right to safely continue the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe. A difficult decision, made this Wednesday, November 4th, in consultation with Samuel Tual, president of the Actual Group. articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER BULLETIN - NOVEMBER 4th
articles.excerpt: This Wednesday, November 4th, three days after the start of the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, the weather situation is very complex in the Atlantic, with anticyclonic ridges and low-pressure areas. A low-pressure system will rapidly deepen in the coming hours near the Azores.

articles.title: The Maxi Banque Populaire XI capsized last night off the Azores, Armel is safe.
articles.excerpt: Le Maxi Banque Populaire XI a chaviré cette nuit au large des Açores, Armel est en sécurité

articles.title: Finding the limits
articles.excerpt:
Corentin Horeau (MACSF) is reaping the rewards of his tactical choice. As the only IMOCA skipper to break through the trough yesterday, he holds a lead of over 130 miles this morning.
Jérémie Beyou (Charal) has decided to withdraw from the race for medical reasons. Charles Caudrelier (Maxi Edmond de Rothschild) is heading back to Lorient following damage to his port-side foil. Anthony Marchand (Actual Ultim 4) has reached Galway, Ireland.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - The Ocean Fifty Elvest has capsized
articles.excerpt: On Tuesday at 21:05 UTC, the Ocean Fifty Elvest, skippered by Matthieu Perraut, capsized while 400 miles north of the Azores.

articles.title: Knitting knots and sitting ducks
articles.excerpt: It was veteran French meteo expert Jean Yves Bernor who surveyed the Atlantic pre-start and described the picture ahead as ‘a mess’. And surveying the scene this Tuesday evening he seems to be very much correct. It is the leading group of IMOCAs which has so far suffered most, the exception seeming to be the wily Corentin Horeau (MACSF) who has been able to gybe down a corridor of breeze and he has seen a slender lead multiply to over 100 miles.

articles.title: Charles Caudrelier and the Maxi Edmond de Rothschild diverted to Lorient
articles.excerpt: Mardi 3 novembre 2026 - Il y a quarante-huit heures, le dimanche 1er novembre à 13h02 au large de Saint-Malo, le nouveau Maxi Edmond de Rothschild s’élançait sur sa première grande course, huit mois seulement après sa mise à l’eau.

articles.title: Decision Time
articles.excerpt: With the first big transition zone of the race behind them, the ocean giants of Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe, the Ultim class, are making rapid progress on a southwesterly course. SVR Lazartigue’s Tom Laperche is setting a pace which Armel Le Cléac’h (Maxi Banque Populaire XI) seems to have struggled to match today, not least as SVR has had the better, stronger breeze.

articles.title: Race progress update: refueling!
articles.excerpt: After 48 hours of racing, bodies are tired but minds are working at full speed as it's already time for the first strategic decisions to determine the opportune moment to turn south. Between meals and naps, a midday update on the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe fleet.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Fabien Delahaye, aboard LEGALLAIS, abandons the race due to an ankle injury
articles.excerpt: This morning around 6 a.m., while sailing in 25 knots of wind and very rough seas, Fabien Delahaye injured his ankle while going to lower his spinnaker on the foredeck of his Class40. Since then, the skipper of LEGALLAIS, who is sailing for the fourth season under the colors of the Normandy-based company, has been in contact with the race doctor. The pain is extremely intense, and he is unable to put any weight on his foot.

articles.title: the first light with the sailors 🌊
articles.excerpt: Après une nouvelle nuit d'engagement total, les premières lueurs de l'aube éclairent les cockpits. Entre veille météo, réglages millimétrés et manœuvres, les skippers partagent un aperçu de leur quotidien au large.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 3
articles.excerpt: Ce mardi 3 novembre, 2 jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, un puissant anticyclone reste centré sur le nord des Iles Britanniques et intéresse encore une grande partie de la flotte mais un front perturbé concerne les marins les plus à l’ouest.

articles.excerpt: During the night, Armel contacted his team after encountering damage to one of his two rudders.
